subject: Civil Engineering
title: Seismic Building Codes
description: A quick, practical guide to Seismic Building Codes.

hook.text: Earthquakes don't kill people. Badly built buildings do. Codes prevent that.

buildup.text: Building codes specify minimum seismic forces that every structure must be designed to resist.

discovery.text: The design force depends on seismic zone, soil type, building height, and structural system.

twist.text: Life safety is the minimum standard — the code allows damage but prevents collapse.

climax.text: After every major earthquake, codes are updated. Each disaster teaches new lessons.

punchline.text: The building code is written in lessons from collapsed structures.

quiz.question: What is the minimum performance goal of seismic building codes?
options: Zero damage to the building during any earthquake
Life safety — preventing collapse and protecting occupants even if the building is damaged
Full functionality immediately after the earthquake ends

details.summary: Seismic building codes specify minimum design requirements for structures in earthquake-prone regions, including seismic force levels, structural system limitations, detailing requirements for ductility, and drift limits.
details.whyItMatters: Building codes are the primary tool for preventing earthquake casualties. Countries with enforced seismic codes experience dramatically fewer deaths from earthquakes of similar magnitude than those without them.
takeaways: Codes define seismic design force based on hazard, soil type, and building importance
Ductile detailing requirements ensure structures deform without sudden collapse
Life safety, not damage prevention, is the primary performance objective for most codes

faq.question: Do seismic building codes guarantee that buildings survive earthquakes undamaged?
faq.answer: No. Most codes are designed for life safety, meaning buildings should not collapse but may be damaged beyond repair in the design earthquake. Only essential facilities like hospitals and fire stations are designed to remain functional.

faq.question: Why do some earthquake-prone countries still have inadequate seismic codes?
faq.answer: Developing and enforcing codes requires technical expertise, institutional capacity, and political will. Construction cost increases of 5 to 15% for seismic design face resistance in low-income countries.
